Subject: [URGENT] Sustained 5xx spike + p95 latency increase — dedicated pool appears saturated

Kim,

We’re seeing a sustained wave of 5xx errors and p95 tail latency jumping from ~220ms to ~1.8s across our reserved endpoints starting at ~08:30 PDT. Overall throughput to our reserved capacity shows a 28% drop vs the committed baseline (token/sec) and the dashboard indicates the dedicated GPU pool for our reservation at >95% utilization.

This is impacting customer-facing inference and causing order-processing timeouts. We opened an incident on our side (INC-7281) and attached a small slice of request logs in the ZIP. Can you escalate — we need an immediate mitigation (failover path or temporary burst authorization) and an ETA for resolution. This is in production for our core payments flow; legal will want details if SLAs are breached.

Attaching: request-logs-20270914.zip, sample_traces.txt

From: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, naomi_feldman@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 09:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: [URGENT] Sustained 5xx spike + p95 latency increase — dedicated pool appears saturated

Short technical readout (initial):
- Symptom: sudden rise in 5xx errors coincident with an increase in KV-cache pressure from a large batch job (non-prod user mistakenly sent a production routing key) — this caused persistent GPU memory pressure and degraded kernel scheduling for the reserved pool.
- Observed: sustained dedicated GPU utilization >95%, queue length growth on our token dispatcher, and OOM-retries on the model worker processes.

Mitigations in-flight:
1) Temporary re-routing: we can programmatically redirect non-critical endpoints (analytics/preview) to hosted shared instances within 5 minutes, which will free ~18% capacity.
2) Burst allocate: if billing authorizes, we can add a 24-hour burst of reserved compute to restore headroom (~+40% capacity) within ~12 minutes of provisioning.
3) Short-term model rollback: recommend rolling back the most recent model variant (v4.7 -> v4.6) for the reserved endpoints to avoid the memory-heavy kernel path; that’s a ~3–5 minute config flip with immediate effect.

Requesting: AUTH for reroute + model rollback now (low-risk) and Marcus to authorize burst so we have extra runway while we investigate root cause and prevent recurrence.

Hannah Schmitt
SRE, Serving Runtime, Redwood Inference
